findings.reason: §5 must name `load_packaged_signal_map` as the loader for the JT-60SA maps (or state why it cannot be), or the map-loading half of §5 lands against an unnamed mechanism.
findings.text: the plan places pulse signal maps at `imas_ambix/data/maps/jt-60sa/<system>.json` (§1/§5) but names no loader for them, while `load_packaged_signal_map(machine, system)` already keyed by machine and system is the mechanism that reads the MAST maps; a plan that does not cite it risks authoring a parallel loader

findings.reason: §4's "zero machine-name branches" done-when is only checkable if the plan names every existing machine-keyed angle owner, and this one is absent from the text.

findings.text: the §3 extractor re-implements the remote-batch layer codex already owns (`imas_codex/remote/executor.py`, `ssh_worker.py`, `serialization.py`, and `scripts/enumerate_edas.py`), which the plan names and declines to import; the owner to extend is codex's remote layer

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new concern is one deep entry point rather than a spread of wrappers: `selene_deck.py` one converter entry point, the §3 extractor "one batch-fetch function and one cache writer", the §2 exporter "one public function", and §7 reuses the §3 transport/cache for the EQDB reader rather than adding a second path; `read_geometry_table` remains the one acquisition route.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan retires `description_reader._supply_declared_probe_angles`'s `machine == "mast"` branch but leaves the second MAST-keyed angle owner at `gs/geometry.py` unnamed; the §3 extractor is a named duplicate of codex's remote layer that the plan already answers in its own text.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — against this week's 0 public_definitions, 0 cli_options, 0 mcp_views, 0 refusal_families, every section that adds surface accounts for it in its own text: §2 "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter", §3 extractor "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today" and the cache "adds no `ambix data` command", §4 the two store-addressing keys "retire nothing, because the catalogue had no addressing slot" while the probe-angle key "retires the machine branch", §7 the EQDB reader and the two record fields each "retire nothing" with a stated absence.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites its prior art densely and correctly (VirtualZarrView, cocos_convention.score_convention, description_identity, efit_referee.judge_geometry, MachineArtifactGeometrySource, DIIID loader, paths.py owners, tokamap export, eddb/selene_deck — all verified present), but it never names `load_packaged_signal_map` (imas_ambix/data/signal_map.py:631), the existing per-machine-per-system signal-map loader that should read the §5 JT-60SA signal maps, nor the second MAST-keyed directed-probe-angle owner at imas_ambix/gs/geometry.py:842.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the layers that could have been thin wrappers each carry an explicit justification for existing instead of extending: the tokamap exporter is forward-only with no reverse claim (§2), the extractor exists because ambix has no remote reader and importing codex's layer would make it a runtime dependency (§3), and the deck reaches the engine through the existing netCDF engine with a receipt rather than a new store engine (§4 decision `description-source-engine`).
